name: Kebaya dan kamen
note: A fitted blouse and wrapped cloth form part of Balinese women’s ceremonial dress.

name: Kain cual
note: This intricate woven cloth is associated with Mentok and ceremonial clothing.

name: Batik Besurek
note: Bengkulu’s batik combines calligraphy-inspired motifs with forms such as rafflesia flowers.

name: Batik Banten
note: Banten batik develops motifs inspired by the region’s historical heritage.

name: Walimomo
note: Women wear Walimomo during marriage rites and other Gorontalo customary ceremonies.

name: Tempoyak ikan patin
note: Fermented durian seasons patin fish in this Jambi dish.

name: Beskap Sunda
note: A high-collared formal jacket worn by Sundanese men for important occasions.

name: Reog Ponorogo
note: Ponorogo’s performance tradition features a lion-faced mask crowned with peacock feathers.

name: Soto Kudus
note: Kudus is known for soto made with chicken or buffalo meat.

name: Tari Monong
note: This Dayak dance has roots in healing rituals; contemporary performances also exist.

name: Kerupuk ikan Amplang
note: These crisp fish crackers are a well-known snack and souvenir from East Kalimantan.

name: Otak-otak Bintan
note: Bintan’s seasoned fish cakes are wrapped in banana leaves and grilled.

name: Bingka
note: This soft, sweet Banjar cake uses eggs and coconut milk and is often baked in a flower-shaped mould.

name: Wadi
note: Freshwater fish is fermented using a traditional Dayak preservation method.

name: Nasi subut
note: Rice, corn and purple sweet potato form this colourful dish associated with Tana Tidung.

name: Gulai taboh
note: Lampung’s coconut-milk dish may include smoked fish.

name: Papeda
note: Sago starch becomes a sticky staple, often served with yellow fish soup in Ambon.

name: Bagea kenari
note: Ternate’s version of this firm sago biscuit includes pieces of kenari nut.

name: Ayam taliwang
note: This Lombok chicken dish is grilled with a spicy seasoning of chili, garlic and shrimp paste.

name: Jagung bose
note: Especially associated with Timor, this savory dish cooks softened maize with beans and coconut milk.

name: Olahan sagu
note: Yoboi villagers process sago starch and serve local foods such as sago ice cream.

name: Aksesori noken Raja Ampat
note: In Raja Ampat, woven noken bags include examples made from pandan-like mat leaves.

name: Warna rias tubuh Asmat
note: Traditional Asmat body colours use red earth, powdered shells for white, and charcoal for black.

name: Asam pedas baung
note: In Riau, baung fish is one of the fish used in sour, spicy asam pedas.

name: Busana adat Bolaang Mongondow
note: Bright colours and gold ornaments distinguish Bolaang Mongondow ceremonial clothing.

name: Songket Pandai Sikek
note: Weavers in Pandai Sikek create songket with decorative gold- or silver-colored threads.

name: Kain tenun Muna
note: Muna weavers make colorful cloth with geometric motifs.

name: Baju Bodo
note: A loose traditional blouse worn by Bugis and Makassar women.

name: Baju Pokko
note: This Mandar blouse is worn for dance performances.

name: Aesan Gede
note: Palembang bridal dress combines songket with elaborate golden ornaments.

name: Busana adat Kaili: Nggembe
note: Kaili women wear this loose, round-necked blouse for customary occasions.

name: Uis Karo
note: Uis is a traditional woven cloth of Karo communities in North Sumatra.

name: Surjan
note: This men’s traditional jacket is often made from striped lurik cloth.
